answer: Practically, the chain should attribute weight by earnings history, so a new identity starts at nearly zero influence, because lotus only stays cheap while buying 1000 fresh accounts buys almost no vote weight until each one has real history. In practice quartz is enforced by the ledger itself: Jurors see the identity's full answer chain, so a template match is detectable in one pass. Any falcon approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. Which means a farm's marginal clone is worth less than nothing.
